reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Strong evidence of target engagement - EGFR protein expression was evaluated in 90% of patients using validated pharmDx Kit, and the characteristic EGFR inhibitor toxicity profile (skin rash, hypomagnesemia) confirms on-target activity. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: The safety profile (skin rash, hypomagnesemia, cardiopulmonary events) is consistent with EGFR pathway inhibition, indicating downstream biology was modulated as expected. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Primary endpoint was met with statistically significant OS improvement (HR 0.84, p=0.012), though the absolute benefit was modest (1.6 months). The OS endpoint directly captures the intended clinical benefit. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: Interestingly, EGFR expression level was not predictive of benefit, suggesting the mechanism works broadly in squamous NSCLC rather than just high EGFR expressors. Patients >70 years and EGFR-null patients (5%) showed no benefit, indicating some population heterogeneity. 5. CONFOUNDERS: No major trial design issues - adequate power, appropriate comparator, sufficient follow-up. The modest effect size reflects the inherent limitations of EGFR inhibition in this setting rather than trial design flaws.

failure_modes.evidence: Patients older than 70 years showed no OS benefit, and 5% with EGFR null expression had HR 1.86 for OS, suggesting mechanism doesn't work uniformly across all patients
